rationale: The sparse-pid probe failed inside the harness, not the target: the pump resolved a message receiver as an array index, so a message to pid 5 indexed past the three-node vector and panicked before any event. This update records that failure as a probe defect, keeps the trim question unresolved, and submits a successor whose routing looks the destination up by get_pid.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt a15df36295234c40a601d42312dfd1ed did not test the target: the test binary panicked at assurance_generated.rs line 63 with 'index out of bounds: the len is 3 but the index is 4' before emitting any CA_EVENT, so the execution parsed no events and the comparison had no applicable result. The fault is in the probe's message pump, which translated a receiver pid into nodes[pid-1]; that works only for contiguous pids starting at 1, and for {1,2,5} a message to pid 5 indexes past a three-element vector. Nothing about trim, the minimum accepted index or the sparse layout is established by this receipt. The successor resolves the destination slot by matching get_pid(), so the sparse run can reach the trim calls and emit its events.
counterevidence: The failure is a harness fault with no bearing on the target behavior; the source-level trim mechanism remains untested rather than refuted.
limitations: No parsed events were produced, so this receipt cannot support or contradict any target claim.
The successor keeps the same three-node {1,2,5} scope, majority quorum, unit batch size and memory storage.

scope.description: Three real OmniPaxos instances with pids 1, 2 and 5, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1; three entries decided, then trim(Some(2)) and trim(None) sampled from the leader, with routing resolved by pid.
assumptions: All produced messages are delivered to their addressed node until none remain.
No ticks are called; leadership is obtained with try_become_leader.
excluded: Snapshots, batching, flexible quorums, reconfiguration and crash recovery.

experiment.prefix: Build pids 1, 2 and 5 with ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,5]} and settle. node1.try_become_leader(); settle. Append Value(1..=3) with a full settle after each. Emit setup with decided and all_accepted_min (minimum get_accepted_idx over the three configured nodes). Call trim(Some(2)) and record trim_ok, error_min and compacted_after_some; call trim(None) and record none_ok and compacted_after_none. Emit trim_result with requested, all_accepted_min, decided and those fields.

comparisons.description: Trim of an index accepted by every configured node should succeed; the predicate is expected to be violated if sparse-pid placeholders pin the minimum to 0.

experiment.revision_reason: The pump resolved a message's receiver with nodes[receiver - 1], which panics for a sparse configuration when pid 5 is addressed in a three-node vector. Routing now finds the destination slot by matching get_pid(); the scenario, inputs, assertions and sampled fields are unchanged.
